title: Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter()
summary: Given a character model (or anything in it), finds the owning Player — the standard bridge from 'some part got touched' to 'which player did it'.

parameters.name: character
parameters.description: The character model. Passing a body part returns nil — pass hit.Parent (the model).

reference.returns: The Player, or nil if the model isn't a current player character.

explanation.whyItExists: Touched events and physics interactions hand you PARTS; gameplay needs the PLAYER.
whenToUse: Touched handlers: who stepped on this pad?
Attributing kills, pickups, zones to players
whenNotToUse: On the hit part itself — pass its Parent model
For NPCs/robots — they're not Players; nil is correct
tips: Always handle the nil case (parts, debris, pets also touch things)
commonMistakes: Assuming non-nil means human — zombies built from player rigs can fool naive checks; combine with your own markers

examples.title: Touch → player attribution
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local character = hit.Parent
    local player = character and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(character)
    if player then
        print(player.Name .. " stepped on the pad")
    end
end)
